lessons.culture: An Iraqi host protests when guests say they must go, and pressing them to stay is politeness, not a real attempt to hold them. Thanks go both ways with "y3atiikum il-3aafya" and "bwujoodkum", and the host often walks the guests to the door or car and waits until they leave.

challenge.title: Hosting or Visiting in Baghdad
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation where you either welcome a guest into your home from the door to the table, or visit someone and take your leave at the end. Use at least one welcome at the door, one phrase about food or drink, and one closing thanks or goodbye.
required_elements: a welcome at the door (e.g. hala w sahla, tfaddal juwwa)
an offer or compliment about food or drink (e.g. shtriid tishrab / tislam iidak)
a closing thanks or goodbye (e.g. y3atiikum il-3aafya / alla wiyyaakum)
